sincere.text: They both said they liked strong coffee, then took one look at the line and left. I didn't see that coming.

partner.text: Page one's in. Funny how the tasting survey never asked when the bus was due.

sincere.text: The guy with the empty tube just asked for the blue one. Never even said the brand name.

partner.text: Page two's in. One showed up with an empty tube, the other showed you a phone. Good luck getting that from search numbers.

sincere.text: I figured he put two in the cart hoping for a deal. Turns out he didn't want to buy what his mom already had.

partner.text: Page three's in. Two bottles in the cart. The order alone couldn't tell us what he was comparing.

sincere.text: That ‘Book Now’ card was already printed. Never crossed my mind those two words might make someone close the tab.

partner.text: Page four's in. The guy just wanted to see out the window, and we nearly asked for his phone number first.

sincere.text: She went to the trouble of washing that old pump and bringing it in, and we couldn't even tell her if she could still use it.

partner.text: Page five's in. If that pump leaks, a bigger tagline isn't going to help.

sincere.text: I nodded along at ‘worried it’ll be too sweet.’ Then I checked the transcript and saw she meant her coworker.

partner.text: Page six is in. Next time the summary says ‘too sweet,’ I’m asking ‘too sweet for who?’

sincere.text: That kid rode all the way home to change before dinner last time. Till you asked, I had no idea it was the fryer smell.

partner.text: Page seven's in. Show up to dinner smelling like fryer oil? I'd take the extra ride too.

sincere.text: The boss circled that checkout screen, and I almost forgot Auntie was the one picking the soy sauce.

partner.text: Page eight is in. You’d never guess from that checkout screen that Auntie picked the yellow cap.

sincere.text: I was so focused on whether the daughter would buy it. Then you asked, and her mom said she just wanted to take the bus to Yongkang Street herself.

partner.text: Page nine's in. I rewound that bit twice. Mom didn't hesitate for a second before taking it out of the cart.
